# PowerShell Gotchas

> Known PowerShell patterns that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors. Load all HIGH entries before writing any PowerShell script.

## Entries

- [Variable quoting in strings](quoting.md): Double quotes expand variables; single quotes are always literal. Use $() for expressions inside strings. HIGH.
- [Error handling with -ErrorAction Stop](error-handling.md): Default error action is Continue -- errors are silently swallowed. Always use -ErrorAction Stop with try/catch and set $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop' at script top. HIGH.
- [Array safety with @() wrapping](array-safety.md): Pipeline results with a single item become a scalar, not an array. Wrap in @() to guarantee array type. HIGH.
- [Runtime module checks instead of #Requires](modules.md): Never use #Requires -Modules; check at runtime with Get-Module -ListAvailable and install if missing. MEDIUM.
- [Always use UTC for date fields](utc-dates.md): [DateTime]::Now is local time. Use [DateTime]::UtcNow for Graph API and any external API that expects UTC. Causes KeyCredentialsInvalidEndDate and similar errors. HIGH.
- [Initialize variables before conditional branches (StrictMode)](strict-mode-variables.md): Under Set-StrictMode -Version Latest, accessing an unset variable throws. Initialize all variables before any if/else branch that might not execute. HIGH.
- [> is redirection and parens can misparse in strings](special-chars-in-strings.md): Bare > in double-quoted strings is parsed as output redirection. Use -> instead. Parentheses around words can also misparse -- use backtick-escape or rephrase. HIGH.
- [Never pass complex scripts inline via -Command from bash](bash-to-powershell.md): Bash expands $variables, $false, $true, $null, and backticks before PowerShell runs. Use a temp .ps1 file with -File instead. HIGH.
- [Feature-detect SDK parameters before using them](feature-detect-params.md): SDK versions add parameters over time. Use (Get-Command).Parameters.ContainsKey() before using optional parameters. MEDIUM.
- [Don't assume catch-block operations will succeed](catch-block-safety.md): Fallback operations in catch blocks can also throw. Use nested try/catch for critical fallbacks. MEDIUM.
- [All Microsoft.Graph.* submodules must be the same version](graph-module-version-mismatch.md): Mixed versions cause assembly loading errors. Check version alignment after installing multiple Graph submodules. HIGH.
- [Old EXO module in user path shadows system-wide version](exo-module-version-shadowing.md): PS7 loads from ~/Documents/PowerShell/Modules first. A stale EXO 2.x there shadows the system-wide 3.x, causing WinRM errors with no hint about the version mismatch. HIGH.
- [System.Web is .NET Framework only -- not in PowerShell 7+](system-web-not-in-pwsh7.md): Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Web and [System.Web.Security.Membership]::GeneratePassword() fail in pwsh because System.Web ships only with .NET Framework. Scripts work in powershell.exe but break in pwsh. Use a hand-rolled Get-Random generator or System.Security.Cryptography.RandomNumberGenerator. HIGH.
- [Comma-wrap return collapses multi-element array when caller does @()](comma-return-collapse.md): `return ,$arr` is meant to prevent unrolling but when the caller does `@(Get-Foo)` it nests the array as element 0 of a 1-tuple. Symptom: paginated function logs show 600+ items added internally but caller sees Count=1. Just return the array without comma. HIGH.
- [MSAL.PS Enable-MsalTokenCacheOnDisk silently in-memory under pwsh 7](msal-disk-cache-pwsh7.md): The disk-cache extension only works under Windows PowerShell 5.1. Under pwsh 7 it prints a WARNING and falls back to in-memory, so every script run prompts for a fresh device code. Run via powershell.exe, roll your own DPAPI cache, or use Az.Accounts. HIGH.
- [Member enumeration on an array returns every element's value](member-enumeration-concatenation.md): Accessing a property on an array (e.g. $orgs.name) returns an array of all elements' values and silently concatenates them in strings/-f/Write-Host. Iterate with an explicit foreach and guard optional properties with PSObject.Properties checks. HIGH.
- [ExchangeOnlineManagement 3.10.0 cmdlets fail on PowerShell 7.6+ with GetResponseHeader error](exo-getresponseheader-pwsh76.md): Connect-ExchangeOnline succeeds but Get-Mailbox and other REST cmdlets throw "HttpResponseMessage does not contain a method named 'GetResponseHeader'" on PS 7.6+. Pin the import to 3.9.2 with -RequiredVersion. HIGH.
- [[IO.Directory]::Delete recursive aborts on the first ACL-denied subdir (not atomic)](io-directory-delete-partial-abort.md): The $true recursive overload throws and STOPS at the first subdir it can't remove (deny ACE, reparse point, locked hive) after already deleting what it reached, leaving a partial husk. For profiles use Remove-CimInstance Win32_UserProfile, or takeown + Remove-Item -Recurse inside a detached Scheduled Task. MEDIUM.
- [ConvertTo-Json truncates at -Depth 2 by default and silently destroys nested config files](convertto-json-depth-truncation.md): ConvertTo-Json defaults to -Depth 2; anything deeper becomes the literal string "System.Object[]" with no error and still-valid JSON, so read-modify-write on a Chromium/Edge Preferences file (1.2MB, 12 levels) silently destroys the profile while reporting success. Use -Depth 100 and gate the write on no "System.Object[]", re-parses cleanly, and size sanity. HIGH.
- [A verification scan that fails to read the file reports "CLEAN"](locked-file-read-false-clean.md): [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes throws on a service-locked file (e.g. wpndatabase.db held by WpnUserService); with $bytes null the needle search finds 0 hits and the script prints CLEAN having read nothing. Read via FileShare::ReadWrite, report INCONCLUSIVE rather than falling through to success, and always add a positive control. HIGH.
- [Add-Type C# referencing System.Drawing fails on modern .NET (type forwarding)](addtype-systemdrawing-type-forwarding.md): Inline C# hits unresolvable CS1069/CS0012 errors (types forwarded into System.Private.Windows.* assemblies); call Bitmap/LockBits/Marshal directly from PowerShell instead, where runtime binding makes forwarding a non-issue. MEDIUM.
- [ConvertFrom-Json is case-INSENSITIVE and throws on valid JSON containing keys that differ only by case](convertfrom-json-case-insensitive-keys.md): JSON is case-sensitive but ConvertFrom-Json deserializes into a case-insensitive dictionary, so a legal {"LOL":..,"lol":..} blows up the ENTIRE parse ("duplicated keys"). Real trigger: Edge Preferences edge_rewards coachmark dicts. The file is not corrupt - do not "repair" it. Use JavaScriptSerializer (5.1, case-sensitive) or ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable (PS7). HIGH.
- [Bitwise -bor / -shl on [byte] operands silently truncates to a byte](bitwise-byte-truncation.md): Combining bytes into a wider value with -bor/-shl keeps the [byte] type and truncates to 8 bits with no error, so 0x6001 becomes 0x01 and every lookup silently misses (empty output, no exception). Cast to [int] or use integer arithmetic. HIGH.
